newsitem.title: USA: Government cracks down on travel scams.
newsitem.headline: Government cracks down on travel scams.

text.p: Federal and state governments cracked down on travel fraud Thursday, taking coordinated legal action against companies that cost consumers billions of dollars annually.

"Travel-related scams are taking off again," the Federal Trade Commission said in announcing "Operation Trip-up," which includes both civil court actions and warnings to consumers on ways to avoid getting taken.
FTC consumer fraud director Jodie Bernstein told a news conference the agency was pursuing five fraudulent firms that had taken the public for $43 million in recent years.
But Bernstein also cautioned consumers to be wary in making travel- and vacation-related purchases, because travel fraud runs into the billions of dollars each year.
She said one way to avoid fraud is to buy vacation and travel services with a credit card, providing some recourse later if promised services are not provided.

"Buy vacation travel only from a business you know, get the details of your vacation and any refund policy in writing before you pay and be wary of pre-paying for multiple years worth of travel," Bernstein said.

One scam that was cited targeted immigrants and promised them "affordable" tickets to their homes in India or Africa. The merchant, "Your Travels and Tours" of Cambridge, Mass., required cash payment immediately, the government said.
One of those who lost money from "Your Travels" was Aatif Aaquil of Detroit, who purchased tickets to visit family in India but never got the tickets, despite repeated phone calls.
"Since then I've been asking for the refund of my money," he told the news conference. "I paid them something like $2,990 and I haven't received a single dollar back as yet."
Soon after the news conference, the FBI arrested the proprietors of "Your Travel" in Cambridge, Abul Khayer and his wife, Umme Salma Momtaz Alam.

The government said it received more complaints about Design Travel of Santa Rosa, Calif., than about any other firm. FTC lawyer Collot Guerard said bank records showed that Design Travel processed $14 million in credit card charges while falsely promising "free vacations."
People paid Design Travel $600 to $900 for a ferry ride from Florida to the Bahamas for a stay in a vermin-infested hotel, Guerard said.
California authorities have a search warrant for records of the firm as they pursue criminal law violations by Design Travel's owner, Roger Dolgin, the FTC said.
The federal government also cracked down on Gold Crown Express and Worldwide Vacation Services, two firms owned by William Ernest Taft, who is in jail in Slidell, La., the FTC said.
Taft's firms operated in various states and allegedly claimed it could sell American time-shares in Europe. Bernstein said there is no market for time-shares anywhere.

World Class Network of Irvine, Calif., allegedly sold so-called "tutorial" kits for people to operate "home-based travel agencies" that supposedly gave people a way of getting low-price tickets. They don't.
Later in the day, the FTC obtained a preliminary injunction against World Class.
Travel Bahamas Tours of Florida and Texas allegedly sold pre-paid certificates for pre-paid stays at world-class hotels, but the hotels had never heard of them.

State attorneys general in California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Massachusetts, Michigan, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Vermont, Washington and Wisconsin joined in targeting the travel fraud, going after some of the same firms as the federal government as well as others.
